sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7 million, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9 million [F6][F7][D241][D292].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth and 36.3% of that year's revenue [D582][D580].
The FY2022 reversal followed as REGEN-COV sales went to zero, a 36.3pp drag, after new SARS-CoV-2 variants proved unsusceptible to the treatment [S49][D585][P7].
Since then growth has slowed to 7.8%, 8.3% and 1.0% in FY2023 to FY2025, with operating margin down 3.2pp in FY2025 to a window low of 24.9% [D342][D391][D440][F30][D453][D749].
The mix has inverted: net product sales fell to 44.0% of revenue in FY2025 from 75.4% in FY2021, while collaboration revenue reached 51.1% [D505][D493][D521].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits contributed 9.3pp of FY2025 growth, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D592][P9].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% in FY2025, a 14.2pp drag, on competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition [D577][D578][P10].
EYLEA HD partly offset that, adding 3.1pp as volumes rose, and Libtayo added 1.7pp [D614][P11][D537].
Operating income fell 10.3% in FY2025 against 1.0% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage [D441][D440].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 sits 9.7pp below the window median of 34.6% and far below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the FY2025 margin as it grew 14.0% to $5,850.2 million, or 40.8% of revenue [D465][D455][X34][D420].
SG&A added 2.0pp back, falling 8.6% on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D466][D456][P5].
Gross margin on net product sales also narrowed on manufacturing investment, inventory write-offs and higher Libtayo amortization [P4].
Net margin held at 31.4% because other income of $1,652.8 million and a 13.9% tax rate cushioned the operating decline [F50][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income in FY2025, and free cash flow of $4,080.5 million was 0.91x [F80][F40][D428][F100][D429].
That is above the window median free-cash-flow conversion of 0.88x, with a 28.4% free-cash-flow margin against a 26.4% median [D763][D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898.4 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16,879.9 million in FY2025, 117.7% of revenue, against a peer median of -50.7% (n=8) [D434][D435][D781].
Total debt was flat at $1,985.9 million and the current ratio 4.13x [F187][F180].
Buybacks of $3,438.6 million plus dividends of $370.3 million consumed 93.3% of free cash flow, cutting diluted shares 5.6% [X137][X140][D436][D437][D459].
That helped diluted EPS grow 8.2% against 2.1% net income growth [D444][D442].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, 30.7pp from the FY2021 peak, and FY2025 set a new window low [R1][F26][F30][D749].
The decline reflects a genuine mix shift toward lower-margin collaboration profit shares and heavy R&D, not a one-off charge [R1].

FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table is a later recast ($5,145.6 million and $6,557.6 million) versus $6,710.8 million and $7,863.4 million as first reported, so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4].
Whether operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the FY2025 window low of 24.9% or extends the four-year slide [F30][D749].
Whether US EYLEA sales stabilize after the 42.4% FY2025 decline, or EYLEA HD growth above the $1,636.9 million FY2025 level offsets further erosion [D577][S64].
Whether R&D as a share of revenue stays above the 34.6% window median, having reached 40.8% in FY2025 [D420][D760].
